inputs.root_cause: The official Jupyter `nbformat` package -- IPYNB's independent oracle -- was never declared in src/python/ipynb/pyproject.toml's test extra, although nine obligation test files import it. In any fresh environment those nine files failed at COLLECTION with ModuleNotFoundError, so `pytest tests/python/ipynb` aborted with 9 collection errors rather than running. The capability reconciler simultaneously reported those capabilities as TESTED, because TESTED is satisfied by a test file existing. The result was that IPYNB's strongest evidence -- its independent-reference tests -- was dead and reported as coverage at the same time.

execution_steps: 1. Read the IPYNB obligation register (68 obligations across 25 capabilities) and the product tree, and built verified inventories by AST scan: 326 public symbols across 19 source modules, 344 tests across 30 test files.

2. Checked the Event 52 capability baseline's claim that IPYNB-CLEAN-001, IPYNB-MERGE-001 and IPYNB-UPGRADE-001 were NOT_STARTED. They are not: cleanup() with CleanupPolicy/ChangeReport, model/diff.py and model/lifecycle.py all exist with corresponding tests. Recorded as a capability-to-symbol mapping artifact that the exact ledger supersedes, rather than propagating it.

3. Generated shared/format-contracts/implementation-evidence/ipynb.yaml with one entry per obligation, mapping only symbols and selectors read out of the real tree. The reconciler fails closed on a symbol that does not exist, which is the correctness check on the mapping.

4. Set every obligation to `partial`, uniformly and deliberately: implementation exists for all 68 and none has been audited against its own declared proof_requirements. Claiming `implemented` before that audit is what proof_requirement_audit_lesson forbids.

5. Hit a schema violation: generated_by was pinned to const:'codex'. Widened it to an enum of known generators rather than mislabelling authorship -- the repository is explicitly multi-agent and its own FF6 controller events carry agent:'claude'. Provenance stays constrained and auditable; it just has to be true.
6. Ran the IPYNB suite and found it did not run at all: 9 collection errors, all ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'nbformat'.
7. Installed nbformat 5.10.4 and re-ran: 337 passed, 50 failed. The 50 failures were not introduced -- they were previously invisible because the files never loaded.
8. Declared nbformat>=5.10 in the ipynb test extra so a fresh checkout cannot silently lose the oracle again, keeping it test-only so the shipped package does not require it.
tests_run: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/python/ipynb -q  # BEFORE: 9 collection errors, suite did not run

evidence.obligations_moved_note: Zero. Every obligation is recorded `partial`; mapping obligations to symbols is not proving them.
evidence.suite_status_change: 9 collection errors (did not run) -> 337 passed, 50 failed
evidence.failure_distribution: version_conversion 10, cell_editor 10, official_schema_validation 9, corpus_integrity 5, production_namespace 3, attachment_management 3, nbformat_core 2, metadata_adapters 2, attachments 2, validation_profiles 1, trust_notary 1, lifecycle_modes 1, forward_compatibility 1
evidence.known_residual: The 50 failures are the real IPYNB work queue and are not fixed here. The exact-obligation reconciler still cannot run for IPYNB because its execution-evidence entry needs a transcript whose recorded result matches reality, and the suite is not green.
